summary:
HIgh Level Summary

- Myanmar ForestWatch is an interactive web application that combines NASA MODIS and VIIRS hotspot observations to help users explore historical fire activity in Myanmar. Developed by Team MASA, it focuses on ten selected reserved forests and the Bago Yoma study area.

- The platform provides an interactive map, forest and sensor filters, a burning-activity calendar, and a simulated 3D drone-style view for exploring selected burn-evidence locations. Machine-learning models support a twelve-month planning outlook based on historical recorded activity.

- The project helps government organizations, conservation teams, researchers, and wildfire responders investigate seasonal and spatial fire patterns. By making satellite observations easier to interpret, Myanmar ForestWatch supports informed forest monitoring and planning.
details:
Project Details
- Myanmar ForestWatch processes historical NASA FIRMS observations through data cleaning, confidence filtering, geographic filtering, and MODIS–VIIRS sensor comparison.
- Our dashboard allows users to explore hotspot distributions, seasonal patterns, and forest-specific observations.
- A simulated 3D drone-style orbit provides an immersive view of selected burn-evidence locations.

Technical Implementation
- The application uses React, TypeScript, and MapLibre for visualization. Python supports data processing and model training using XGBoost, Random Forest, Logistic Regression, and a seasonal baseline. These models support a twelve-month planning outlook.

Our Aim
The project aims to make satellite fire information accessible for monitoring and planning mainly for government organizations and fire response teams. Further work includes validating provisional forest boundaries and independently reviewing burn evidence.
